NFL DFS Tight End Rankings: Week 8 (DraftKings)

DraftKings main slate · Sunday, November 1 · 11 games · By Chris Spags · · Numbers as of October 29, 9:10 AM ET

Trey McBride is the top-projected tight end on the Week 8 DraftKings main slate at 18.3 DraftKings points for $7,400, at Dallas. Brock Bowers (16.4, $7,600) and Sam LaPorta (12.8, $5,100) are next.

Brenton Strange returns the most per dollar among tight ends projected for at least 7 points: 2.72 projected points per $1,000 at $4,000.

Every projection is a SPAGS model estimate from the October 29, 9:10 AM ET run of the Splash Play NFL model. This page updates each time the main-slate numbers are published.

Tight ends to know in Week 8

Trey McBride, ARI at DAL ($7,400)

Trey McBride carries the highest SPAGS model projection at the position, 18.3 DraftKings points at $7,400. That is 1.9 points clear of Brock Bowers. The model gives him 10.9 targets on 39.7 routes. The salary works out to 2.48 projected points per $1,000, 5th of 19 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations McBride averaged 18.5 points with a simulated floor of 4.7 and a ceiling of 46.6, and he holds 11% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Arizona is a 6-point underdog on the road against Dallas, with an implied team total of 24.25 in a game totaled at 54.5.

Brock Bowers, LV at NYJ ($7,600)

Brock Bowers projects 2nd at the position with 16.4 DraftKings points at $7,600. The model gives him 7.8 targets on 32.0 routes. The salary works out to 2.16 projected points per $1,000, 15th of 19 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Bowers averaged 16.4 points with a simulated floor of 3.4 and a ceiling of 40.9, and he holds 7% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Las Vegas is a 1.5-point underdog on the road against the Jets, with an implied team total of 22 in a game totaled at 45.5.

Value: Brenton Strange, JAX vs IND ($4,000)

Brenton Strange projects for 10.9 DraftKings points at $4,000, which works out to 2.72 points per $1,000 of salary. That is the best rate of any player priced in the cheaper half of the 19 tight ends the model projects for 7 or more points. The model gives him 4.8 targets on 21.1 routes. Across 10,000 simulations Strange averaged 10.7 points with a simulated floor of 0.5 and a ceiling of 31.9, and he holds 12% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Jacksonville is a 7.5-point favorite at home against Indianapolis, with an implied team total of 27 in a game totaled at 46.5.
